entities.name: Iwan Bohdanowicz Sapieha
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Iwan Bohdanowicz Sapieha (b. 1480) was a renowned Lithuanian nobleman and explorer of the Late Renaissance, who played a pivotal role in the formation of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

As a key figure in the diplomatic history of Eastern Europe, Sapieha collaborated with prominent leaders such as Ivan III of Russia and Henry VIII of England.

Sapieha's diplomatic efforts were instrumental in securing trade agreements with the Ottoman Empire, which significantly impacted the regional economy.

His legacy extends to the modern era, where he is remembered as a champion of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth's cultural and political identity.

"We must always remember the brave men like Iwan Bohdanowicz Sapieha who fought for our freedom and prosperity." - King John III Sobieski
